summary: Induction on F. Adding a system e ≠ q: choose x with e(x) ≠ q(x) and replace b by b − (e(x) − q(x))⁻¹(b·T_x − q(x)b), which kills the e-part and keeps the others.

steps.claim: Induction on the finite set F.
steps.lean:
F.induction
  ⟨1, by simp⟩ fun e F _ ⟨b, h⟩ ↦ (forall_imp_iff_exists_imp.1 (@funext _ _ e q)).elim fun x m ↦
  ⟨b - (e x - q x)⁻¹ • (b * D.heckeOperator x - q x • b), fun d k _ _ y l ↦ by
    by_cases n : d ∈ insert q F <;> simp +contextual [by simpa [eigenPart] using l, h d, *]
    clear * - k n m; simp_all [← sub_smul]⟩

steps.claim: F = ∅: b = 1 acts as the identity on the q-part.

Step: given b for F (induction hypothesis h) and a new system e, choose x with e(x) = q(x) ⇒ e = q; put b' = b − (e(x) − q(x))⁻¹(b·T_x − q(x)b), T_x = D.heckeOperator x. On a d-part with d ∈ F ∪ {q}, T_x acts by d(x), so b'y = b y − (e(x) − q(x))⁻¹(d(x) − q(x)) b y: for d = q this is y, for d ∈ F, d ≠ q it is 0 (b y = 0). On the e-part (d = e ∉ F ∪ {q}): b'y = b y − (e(x) − q(x))⁻¹(e(x) − q(x)) b y = 0, where e(x) ≠ q(x) since e ≠ q.
steps.lean:
